judged_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod safeParse result wrapper ({success, data}), but this call site stores that wrapper directly as the credential key (data: { key }), whereas the previous googleCredentialSchema.parse(...) stored the parsed token object itself. After the first token refresh the google calendar credential's key in the DB becomes {success:true, data:{...}} instead of {access_token, expiry_date, refresh_token}; every subsequent read of credential.key.access_token/.refresh_token (including the next refresh's googleCredentials.refresh_token) returns undefined and Google Calendar sync breaks for that user until re-authentication — and this fires in the default credential-sharing-disabled configuration, not just sync mode.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (with `{ success, data, error }`), not the parsed token payload. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh flow changed from `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` (payload) to `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema); await prisma.credential.update({ data: { key }})`, which would persist the wrapper object as `credential.key`. That would break subsequent reads expecting `credential.key.access_token` / `refresh_token`. This occurs regardless of credential-sharing mode because the function always uses `safeParse` (either `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse` or `schema.safeParse`).
